subject: history_social
passage: Along the southern coast of Sri Lanka, toddy tappers harvest the sap of coconut palms, which is drunk fresh or fermented and distilled into arrack. Rather than climb down and up each tree in turn, a tapper moves from one crown to the next along ropes strung high above the ground. The sap that collects overnight in clay pots tied beneath the cut flower ______ to be gathered before the morning sun warms it, so the work begins in darkness. The job demands balance, a head for heights, and a knowledge of each tree's yield that is usually passed from father to son.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject of the sentence is "The sap that collects overnight in clay pots tied beneath the cut flower stalks," and its verb is "has to be gathered." Everything between "sap" and "stalks" tells which sap is meant, so it is part of the subject, and no punctuation may separate a subject from its verb.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon must join two independent clauses, but "The sap … flower stalks" has no main verb.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A single dash here would cut the subject off from its verb; there is no opening dash for it to close.
explanation.C: Correct. The subject "The sap … flower stalks" connects directly to its verb "has" with no punctuation.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A single comma cannot separate a subject from its verb; nothing before it opened a pair of commas.
